{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q005_cupredoxin_function_transfer","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, plastocyanin/azurin-like proteins, ephrin ectodomains, and the N-terminal domain of PAD4 are not in the same narrow family, but they are sibling families inside the same homologous superfamily: class b, All beta proteins; fold b.6, Cupredoxin-like; superfamily b.6.1, Cupredoxins, SUNID 49503. The family split is b.6.1.1 Plastocyanin/azurin-like, SUNID 49504; b.6.1.5 Ephrin ectodomain, SUNID 74874; and b.6.1.6 Peptidylarginine deiminase Pad4, N-terminal domain, SUNID 110107. SCOPe marks homology as implied at the b.6.1 superfamily and below, while the parent b.6 fold alone does not imply homology; therefore the defensible inference is a distant cupredoxin-superfamily relationship, not interchangeable family membership. Copper binding and electron-transfer activity should stay with experimentally supported blue-copper/cupredoxin families such as plastocyanin/azurin-like unless the ephrin or PAD4 protein itself has metal-site residue and functional evidence. An ephrin ectodomain or PAD4 N-terminal domain can use the b.6.1 relationship as a remote structural/homology template signal for the beta-sandwich core, but cross-family representative choice is unsafe for transferring copper ligands, redox chemistry, active sites, or detailed surface biology.","evidence_used":["/api/v1","/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=plastocyanin&limit=10","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=azurin&limit=10","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=ephrin&limit=10","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=PAD4&limit=10","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/49503/children?limit=20","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/49503/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/49502/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/49504/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/74874/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/110107/parents"]}]}
